metadata.disease_context: Cardiac hypertrophy / Heart failure drug repurposing
metadata.dgidb_api_note: DGIdb API blocked in China; data gathered via literature mining of DGIdb-derived publications + direct web scraping of DGIdb drug pages

OGT.role_in_cardiac_disease: O-GlcNAcylation is a double-edged sword: loss causes HF via ISR activation; excess causes dilated cardiomyopathy. Moderate O-GlcNAcylation is cardioprotective. OGT inhibition in endothelial cells proposed for HFpEF.
OGT.key_finding: OGT is primarily a research target; no approved drugs directly target OGT. OSMI-1/OSMI-4 are the best-characterized tool inhibitors. Paradoxically, both OGT activators (Thiamet-G) and inhibitors (OSMI-1) show context-dependent cardiac effects. An OGT inhibitor patent exists specifically for HFpEF (5S-GlcNHex).

top_candidates.cardiac_evidence: Cardioprotective in I/R via MG53 O-GlcNAcylation
Blunts hypertrophy; systemic administration possible (Rett syndrome mouse model)
Delayed HF progression in OGT-KO mice - most promising downstream target

RELA.role_in_cardiac_disease: Chronic NF-kB activation drives inflammation, fibrosis, pyroptosis, and adverse remodeling in HF. Inhibition is broadly cardioprotective in preclinical models.
RELA.key_finding: NF-kB is the most druggable target among the 5 genes. Multiple approved drugs (empagliflozin, statins, pimobendan) already show NF-kB inhibitory activity. Proteasome inhibitors (bortezomib/carfilzomib) inhibit NF-kB but are CARDIOTOXIC - not suitable for cardiac repurposing.

top_candidates.cardiac_evidence: Class I HF recommendation; suppresses NF-kB/NLRP3 pathway; activates Nrf2
Direct NF-kB inhibition; reduces HF hospitalization in dogs by ~15 months (EPIC trial)
Inhibits TLR4/NF-kB; pleiotropic anti-inflammatory; extensive CV outcomes data
Reduced MACE in HFpEF (STEP-HFpEF); inhibits NF-kB

NFE2L2.role_in_cardiac_disease: Master regulator of antioxidant defense. Nrf2 deficiency aggravates cardiac hypertrophy, fibrosis, and HF. Activation is broadly cardioprotective via HO-1, NQO1, and other antioxidant genes.
NFE2L2.key_finding: Nrf2 is a highly druggable target with multiple natural and synthetic activators. Bardoxolone methyl (Phase 3) showed efficacy but caused fluid retention/HF in susceptible patients. Sulforaphane (Phase 2 for HFpEF) has the best safety profile. SGLT2 inhibitors activate Nrf2 as part of their cardioprotective mechanism.

top_candidates.cardiac_evidence: Active trial for HFpEF; extensive preclinical CV protection data; excellent safety
BEACON terminated for HF signal; ongoing trials exclude at-risk patients; SAKIGAKE designation
Activates Nrf2/ARE signaling; reduces oxidative stress in diabetic cardiomyopathy
Cardioprotective in ISO-induced cardiac injury; regulates ferroptosis via Nrf2

SPP1.role_in_cardiac_disease: Pro-fibrotic matricellular protein. Elevated in cardiac hypertrophy, fibrosis, and HF. Binds CD44 and integrins. SPP1 knockout reduces fibrosis; silencing attenuates atrial fibrillation and adverse remodeling.
SPP1.key_finding: DGIdb identifies 6 approved drugs interacting with SPP1 (tacrolimus, ponatinib, bosutinib, dasatinib, doxorubicin, zanubrutinib), but most are repurposed from oncology. The anti-TREM2-siSPP1 antibody-siRNA conjugate is the most cardiac-specific approach. OPN aptamers show promise in preclinical cardiac models.

top_candidates.cardiac_evidence: 70-90% Spp1 silencing in TREM2+ macrophages; suppressed AF in mice
Attenuated remodeling and fibrosis post-TAC at both early (4wk) and late (12wk) stages
Top molecular docking hit for OPN binding; network proximity-based repurposing for HCM+PH
DGIdb drug for SPP1; more favorable CV safety profile vs older BTK inhibitors

CD44.role_in_cardiac_disease: Receptor for osteopontin (SPP1). CD44-OPN interaction drives cardiac fibrosis, inflammation, and arrhythmias. CD44-/- mice show reduced ventricular arrhythmias in HF. CD44 regulates Epac1-mediated Ca2+ handling abnormalities.
CD44.key_finding: CD44 is less drugged than other targets. Anti-CD44 antibodies (RG7356, bivatuzumab) showed limited efficacy as monotherapy. Downregulation by statins (simvastatin) is an indirect approach. SPP1-CD44 axis interruption is more promising than CD44 blockade alone. First direct cardiac evidence: CD44 inhibition reduces ventricular arrhythmias in HF (J Biomed Sci 2023).

top_candidates.cardiac_evidence: CD44 inhibition reduces VAs in HF mouse models; anti-arrhythmic potential
Downregulates CD44; pleiotropic benefits in CV disease via combined NF-kB + CD44 pathways
Proof of concept for CD44 druggability; primarily oncology indication currently

cross_target_patterns.SPP1-CD44_axis: SPP1 (osteopontin) is the primary ligand for CD44. Interrupting this interaction is a convergent therapeutic strategy that affects both targets simultaneously. Anti-TREM2-siSPP1 and OPN aptamers are the most specific approaches.
cross_target_patterns.NF-kB_Nrf2_crosstalk: NF-kB (RELA) and Nrf2 (NFE2L2) have antagonistic pathways. NF-kB activation suppresses Nrf2, while Nrf2 activation inhibits NF-kB. Bardoxolone methyl and empagliflozin simultaneously activate Nrf2 and suppress NF-kB.
cross_target_patterns.SGLT2_inhibitors_multi-target: Empagliflozin and dapagliflozin simultaneously: (a) suppress NF-kB/NLRP3 (RELA pathway), (b) activate Nrf2/ARE (NFE2L2 pathway), (c) inhibit NHE1 in cardiomyocytes. This multi-target mechanism may explain their class-leading HF efficacy.
cross_target_patterns.repurposable_approved_drugs: Empagliflozin, dapagliflozin, atorvastatin, simvastatin, semaglutide, pimobendan (veterinary), and sulforaphane (supplement) are the most clinically viable options for cardiac hypertrophy/HF drug repurposing among the 5 genes studied.

risk_notes.cardiotoxic_drugs_to_avoid: Bortezomib and carfilzomib inhibit NF-kB but are CARDIOTOXIC (4-17% HF incidence). Doxorubicin has SPP1 interaction but is CARDIOTOXIC. Ponatinib has vascular occlusion and HF risk. These should NOT be considered for cardiac repurposing.
risk_notes.bardoxolone_fluid_retention: Bardoxolone methyl caused increased HF hospitalizations in BEACON trial (HR 1.83). Fluid retention mechanism involves endothelial Nrf2 activation affecting sodium/water handling. Careful patient selection (excluding BNP>200 or prior HF) reduces risk to ~2%.
risk_notes.ogt_inhibition_context_dependent: OGT inhibition may be beneficial in HFpEF (endothelial mechanism) but harmful in I/R injury (loss of cardioprotective O-GlcNAcylation). Context and cell-type specificity are critical.
